hook_text: The rand's price is set by two queues. Learn to read them and every currency headline makes sense.
clip_script: Everything you buy has a price in rands. Here's the loop nobody explains: the rand ITSELF has a price — about eighteen rand per dollar — and it moves for the same reason bread's price moves. Buyers and sellers. Picture two queues at a counter. Queue one is BUYING dollars with rands: the fuel importer, the shop bringing in phones, the family paying overseas university fees. Queue two is SELLING dollars for rands: the mine shipping coal to India, the wine estate paid in euros, German tourists at the waterfront, foreign funds buying our bonds. Long queue buying, short queue selling? The dollar gets dearer — the rand WEAKENS. Reverse the queues and the rand FIRMS. Now read the news with it. Oil price spikes: importers need more dollars — buy-queue grows — rand weakens. Foreign funds love our bonds: dollars pour into the sell queue — rand firms. Load-shedding scares investors: sell queue empties — rand weakens. Three headlines, one picture. And who controls the price? In South Africa — nobody. The rand floats, and the queues decide. Bumpy, but honest.
visual_style: A bank counter drawn as two snaking queues of tiny characters — an oil tanker, a phone box, a coal truck, a tourist with a camera — swelling and shrinking as a big R-per-dollar price board ticks up and down above them.
pacing: Quick introductions of each queue member, then rapid-fire headline tests, landing on a steady closing line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain any rand headline — plus the balance of payments behind it — in two sentences.
